answer.answer: To check whether a shuttle has the right speed, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1], and the shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2]. A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B [3]. The shuttles should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee [4], and all available speeds shall be tested from both ends of the court [5]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit, including the strength of shot and trajectory, and whether they were hit from the correct location over the back line [6]. The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct [7].
